title: fastpath: introduce safe-mode fallback + precision toggle gating for kernel fast-paths
author: Diego Ramirez
description: Motivation: some recent fast-path optimizations (half-precision kernels, aggressive kernel fusion) improved median throughput but exposed correctness regressions on a small subset of model shapes and attention patterns and caused increased tail failures when mixed-precision boundary conditions were hit. This PR introduces a conservative 'safe-mode' fallback and a precise gating mechanism for precision toggles so the runtime can prioritize correctness when needed while still benefiting from fast-paths in the common case. Design summary: 1) add a SafeMode flag that can be enabled cluster-wide, per-deployment, or per-request via metadata. When enabled, the runtime disables non-validated kernel variants and uses validated reference kernels for sensitive ops. 2) implement a precision gating layer in kernel_selector that tracks model/operator characteristics (sequence length, kv-cache usage, head-dim alignment) and uses a short circuit to avoid selecting half-precision fused kernels when conditions predict numerical instability. 3) extend scheduler/continuous-batching to tag batches with a "fastpath_allowed" bit derived from request metadata + kernel_selector decisions so batching doesn't accidentally combine safe and fast requests. 4) KV cache: ensure cache key format includes precision-mode to avoid cache poisoning between fast/safe modes. 5) conservative rollout: default off for hosted; opt-in via feature flag for internal perf experiments, and a staged rollout for Dedicated. Changeset summary: - runtime/kernel_selector: new gating logic, unit-tested heuristics and telemetry counters (fastpath_allowed/denied). - runtim e/kernels: mark a subset of half-precision kernels with a new attribute 'experimental_fastpath' and add runtime checks. - scheduler/continuous_batcher: propagate request fastpath_allowed and avoid cross-mode batching. - kvcache: cache key now includes precision_mode token and we add a migration-safe prefix. - tests: updated unit and integration tests, added a new perf microbenchmark harness and a flaky-resiliency test to reproduce earlier failure conditions. - docs: internal runtime/README and rollout playbook. Performance and correctness tradeoffs: internal microbenchmarks show the following: when safe-mode disabled and fastpath enabled, median token throughput improves by ~22% and p95 latency improves ~12% on 8xA100; but under adversarial sequences the failure rate increases from 0.01% to 0.8%. With safe-mode enabled the failure rate returns to baseline (<0.02%) while median throughput drops ~6% versus fully fastpath. CI/Testing notes: initial CI run showed a flaky kernel test (kernel_matrix_fusion_test) failing on a single builder; added transient guard in tests and reran CI. All checks are green including the perf-canary job which records the perf/regression deltas used for rollout decisions. Rollout plan: 1) merge behind feature flag. 2) Enable for internal staging with telemetry sampling (10%) for 1 week. 3) If no regressions observed, enable for Dedicated customers behind opt-in and add documentation. Related work: follows up on pr-21487 and pr-23645 which added earlier fastpath optimizations and safe-mode prototypes. Checklist: [x] unit tests; [x] integration tests; [x] perf microbench harness; [x] docs; [x] rollout playbook.
commits_summary: 3 commits: 1) add safe-mode flag, kernel selector gating, and telemetry counters; 2) update scheduler and batching to respect fastpath_allowed bit and fix kv-cache key; 3) tests, docs, and perf harness. Each commit is scoped and includes unit tests where applicable.
review_comments: Anya Patel: We need deterministic fallback behavior across machines. If the gating uses heuristics, add a safety beacon to trace decisions so we can retroactively deduplicate failures.

Diego Ramirez: Added telemetry counters 'fastpath_allowed' and 'fastpath_denied' and an event payload with deterministic inputs (model id, head_dim, seq_len, has_kv). Counters are exposed in runtime/telemetry. PTAL.
Marcus Huang: Please add unit tests for cached entries when precision_mode differs — cache poisoning is a major concern here.
Diego Ramirez: Added integration test kv_cache_safe_mode_test that exercises mixed precision cache reads/writes and verifies isolation.
Liam O'Connor: Perf impact looks acceptable for internal staging, but please document the expected delta and add a canary that compares golden outputs between fastpath and safe kernels.
Diego Ramirez: perf microbench harness added and canary pipeline updated; harness produces token-level diffs and compares numerical deviation thresholds.
ci_checks: Unit tests: passed (one transient failure on first run - kernel_matrix_fusion_test) -> rerun passed
Perf canary: completed (median +22% throughput in fastpath, safe-mode median -6% vs fastpath; p95 latency +12% improvement with fastpath; failure rate regression noted in fastpath experiments)
merge_result: merged (squash) into main by Anya Patel on 2026-02-25. Commit message: 'fastpath: add safe-mode fallback and precision gating to kernel selection; update scheduler and kv-cache to preserve correctness'
release_notes: Runtime: add SafeMode fallback to disable experimental fast-path kernels; kernel_selector: precision gating to avoid FP16 fused kernels on unsafe shapes; scheduler: avoid cross-mode batching; kv_cache: include precision_mode in key to prevent poisoning; opt-in behind feature flag for staged rollout; expected perf tradeoff: up to ~22% median throughput improvement with fastpath enabled; safe-mode reduces throughput by ~6% vs fastpath but restores correctness.
